analysis.title: GOAL Kickstart: Credit pressures drive sharp repricing of monetary policy factor
key_insights: GS's RAI PC2 'Monetary policy' factor fell to -8 last week, the third-lowest level since 2000 (after 2020 and 2022), as downward pressure broadened from rates to credit.

The rates component of the RAI has priced stronger nominal growth since the summer, which weighs on PC2. Widening spreads over the past two weeks pushed the credit component sharply lower, weighing on both PC2 and the headline RAI.
The spread widening was sharpest in Euro Area sovereign spreads, particularly France, but was broad across corporate and EM credit. RAI Credit recorded one of its sharpest weekly declines since 2000.
RAI equity, volatility and FX components were less affected and remain in positive territory. The overall RAI closed at 0.2 on Friday.
Credit stress has spilled into European but not US equities. European equity correlations to sovereign and corporate credit are rising materially while the US equity/CDX correlation remains low.

Historical signal is mixed. In six episodes where PC2 fell to a similar level, subsequent 3-month cross-asset returns were widely dispersed. At the margin, returns were positive for US 10-year TIPS and equities, with 2022 (PC2 negative for almost a year) the key exception.

In five episodes where RAI Credit fell below -2 while RAI ex Credit stayed above -0.5, 3-month return dispersion was wide, but the asymmetry was more positive for duration and less supportive for equities or credit. November 2021 was an exception.
GS is Neutral across asset classes over 3 months but remains OW Equities and UW Credit over 12 months. It stays UW Europe equities and UW EUR IG/HY credit.
Europe's uncertainty sources: tighter French financial conditions and weaker growth, Italy's revised 2027 deficit, Spain's snap election, and upside risk for gas prices into winter.

A rebound in broad risk appetite likely requires rate relief and a higher PC2. The upcoming Q3 earnings season could provide some support. Lower energy prices or further US disinflation could drive a broader 'Goldilocks' repricing.
A policy pivot could help but the hurdle remains high. A meaningful ECB intervention would require more intense and broad-based sovereign stress.
Last week US Core PCE came in below expectations, Euro Area core HICP printed close to consensus, US Manufacturing ISM was unchanged in September, and US labour market data was weaker than consensus.
GS US economists pushed their next and last expected Fed hike to December and still expect 3 cuts until Q1 2028.
GS forecasts S&P 500 at 8000 in 3m, 8300 in 6m and 8700 in 12m from 7723, and US 10-year yield at 4.75% in 3m and 4.45% in 12m from 5.28%.
GS forecasts Brent at $84 in 3m and $77 in 12m from $102, WTI at $79 in 3m and $72 in 12m from $98, and gold at $4,715 in 3m and $5,235 in 12m from $4,145.
S&P GSCI Energy is up 115.0% over 1 year and 6.5% over 1 month. Precious metals fell 3.9% and industrial metals fell 3.8% in the past week.

Valuation: S&P 500 12m forward P/E is 19.3x (53rd percentile of 10 years). US 10-year yield at 5.3% and German 10-year at 3.4% sit at or near the 100th percentile of the past 10 years. EUR HY spread is 348bp, EM hard-currency spread 192bp (93rd percentile).

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 earnings season, lower energy prices or further US disinflation could drive a broad Goldilocks repricing and lift PC2.
tension_points.bear_case: Euro Area sovereign stress is widening credit spreads, and historical analogues show asymmetry less supportive for equities and credit, with 2022 and November 2021 as exceptions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: PC2 does not recover and credit spreads keep widening, with stress extending from Europe to US equities, where the equity/CDX correlation is currently low.
